answer.rationale:
Constraints prune the option set hard: rollback_release is excluded outright because compliance has ruled the security patch non-revertible, so memory_b1's clean-rollback precedent is unusable here regardless of how well it worked on day 18. add_capacity (memory_b3) worked pre-emptively ahead of a known peak; we are already 90 minutes into degradation at peak, and provisioning lead time makes it unlikely to bend the curve in this window. enable_circuit_breaker (memory_b4) contained a *dependency* failure by failing fast — but failing fast on the write path at settlement peak actively sheds customer writes, which is the one thing the primary objective forbids. That leaves regional_failover and route_read_replicas. The single strongest signal in the current situation is that the degradation is confined to the primary region, which points at a regional fault rather than generalized load, and memory_b2 is the direct precedent for exactly that shape. So I want to verify memory_b2 above all others.

What I need from the archive is specifically what memory_b2's consolidated summary omits. "Traffic shifted cleanly and error rates recovered within minutes" is a latency-and-errors claim; it says nothing about write durability. The March degradation may have been read-dominated or off-peak, and the original record may show replication lag, in-flight write reconciliation, or a cutover freeze window that a summary describing a clean shift would smooth away. Today's traffic is write-heavy at daily peak, so a failover that was safe in March could drop or duplicate settlement writes now. That is the load-bearing unknown, and it is the reason I am naming memory_b2 rather than treating it as settled.

I should also flag a bias in the inherited record as a whole: all six memories are success stories. There is no preserved account of an intervention that failed or backfired, which is the signature of survivorship filtering across consolidation cycles. Confidence derived from this corpus should be discounted accordingly, and I should not let the uniform positivity of the archive read as uniform safety.

Intended action: regional_failover, executed as a small guarded test — shift a minority slice of write traffic to the secondary, hold it, and watch replication lag and write-acknowledgement counts before widening. If verification of memory_b2 reveals write-loss or lag caveats in the March record, I fall back to route_read_replicas (memory_b5), which relieves primary contention without ever putting customer writes in transit; it is the weaker fix for a region-confined fault but it cannot lose writes. Either way I want the outcome, including any write reconciliation gaps, written back with the peak-traffic and write-heavy context attached, so the next session inherits the conditions rather than another context-free success line.
